app.title: Whombat (v0.9.0)
app.summary: A person registers a folder of audio recordings as a dataset, sets up an annotation project with instructions and an allowed tag set, and cuts chosen recordings into fixed-length clips that become annotation tasks. The tasks then come up one at a time. On each clip's spectrogram the person draws regions of interest around sound events, tags them from a palette, tags and adds notes to the whole clip, and marks the task completed, rejected or verified, which moves on to the next task. A progress bar, a task map and filters show what is left. The finished project is exported as one JSON file of annotations, ready for training or evaluating machine-learning models.

task.text: Label sound events and whole clips in audio recordings, one task at a time, to build a curated training and evaluation set for machine-learning models.

data.text: Audio recordings with metadata, cut into clips. Each clip carries sound-event annotations (regions on the spectrogram with tags), clip-level tags and notes, and task status badges.
data.item: a fixed-length clip of an audio recording, shown as a spectrogram

stage.text: labelling field recordings as ground truth after they are collected, before model training and evaluation

mechanism.text: A progress bar and task map drive a queue of clips. Each clip's spectrogram is a canvas where boxes, intervals or points are drawn with keyboard modes, and new events take their tags from a tag palette kept at hand. Status buttons or hotkeys record the decision and move to the next task. A project dashboard sums progress and tag counts and exports the annotations.

field.text: sound-event annotation of spectrograms for machine learning in bioacoustics

workflow.name: mark and label regions inside each item of a queue, then mark the item done

steps.here: A dataset is created from a folder of audio files or imported from AOEF JSON. Recordings are picked, filtered or randomly subsampled, and cut into clips of a set duration and overlap, which become tasks.

steps.step: step through items one at a time
steps.here: The progress bar shows tasks as pending, completed, issue or verified. n and p move between tasks, a task map jumps to any task, and filters narrow the queue to a subset of tasks.

steps.step: select a stretch and label it with a category
steps.here: On the clip spectrogram, a starts drawing a box, interval or point, s selects, d deletes, and z zooms. Each new sound event takes every tag in the palette, and Ctrl-drag copies an annotation.

steps.step: attach labels and notes to the whole item
steps.here: Clip tags come from the project's allowed tag set, clicking a palette tag adds it to the clip, and notes can be flagged as issues.

steps.step: decide keep or drop for each item, with a reason
steps.here: g marks a task completed, r rejects it as needing review, and v marks it verified. Each one advances to the next task. Existing badges can be clicked to remove them.

steps.step: track progress toward a target or a total
steps.here: The project dashboard counts completed, pending and issue tasks and shows annotation counts by tag.
A download button saves the whole project as one AOEF JSON file of annotations, statuses and users.

distinctive: Regions of interest are drawn in time and frequency on a spectrogram, as boxes, intervals or single onset points.
Long recordings are cut into fixed-length, possibly overlapping clips, so every task covers a comparable span of audio.
A separate verified status supports a second, independent check of finished annotations.
Annotators can only pick tags registered to the project, which keeps one shared label set across the team.
Metadata and tags from the source recording are shown as context, and clicking one adds it to the palette.
